MUJAHID:v1p376/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p376/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p376/r1.claim: Mujahid compares the scalding drink to pus and blood, black like the dregs of oil.

MUJAHID:v1p376/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p376/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p376/r2.claim: Mujahid says the Fire is a wretched place to gather or meet.

MUQATIL:18:29/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:29/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:29/r1.claim: The truth from the Lord is the Quran.

MUQATIL:18:29/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:29/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:29/r2.claim: Letting people believe or disbelieve is a threat: whoever wishes may affirm the Quran or reject what it contains, as in 41:40.

MUQATIL:18:29/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:29/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:29/r3.claim: A neck of fire emerges and surrounds the unbelievers; this is the enclosing canopy.

MUQATIL:18:29/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:29/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:29/r4.claim: Muhl is black and thick like the sediment of oil; it burns faces when brought near the mouth because of its heat.

MUQATIL:18:29/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:29/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:29/r5.claim: Their drink is evil and their resting place is a bad abode.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p182/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p182/r2.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p182/r2.claim: Qatāda says the truth from God is the Qur'an; the invitation to believe or disbelieve is a threat, with Paradise for belief and Fire for disbelief.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p182/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p182/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p182/r3.claim: God has prepared the Fire for wrongdoers, meaning polytheists; its enclosing wall closes over its people on pillars when they are told to be expelled, like another description of the Fire.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p183#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p183#2/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p183#2/r1.claim: The bad drink and dwelling are threats to those who disbelieve; God will not waste the reward of believers who do good.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p183/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p183/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p183/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd heated a gold-and-silver ewer until it foamed and melted, saying this was the closest worldly likeness to the molten drink.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p183/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p183/r2.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p183/r2.claim: Zayd b. Aslam compares the drink called al-muhl to the dregs of oil.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p183/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p183/r3.speaker: ابن مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p183/r3.claim: Ibn Mujāhid's father says al-muhl is pus and blood.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p183/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p183/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p183/r4.claim: The molten drink burns faces when the damned lean in to drink; the drink and resting place are dreadful.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p183/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p183/r5.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p183/r5.claim: Qatāda says the Fire is a bad dwelling and refuge; Mujāhid's father interprets the word as a gathering place.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p402#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p402#3/r2.speaker: الكلبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p402#3/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi explains the fire's surrounding barrier as smoke encircling the unbeliever, linking it to the three-branched shade passage.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p402#3/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p402#3/r3.speaker: طاوس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p402#3/r3.claim: Tawus says the angels' hearts fluttered when Hell was created and became calm when Adam was created.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p402#3/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p402#3/r4.speaker: عائشة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p402#3/r4.claim: The Prophet said angels were created from light, jinn from smokeless fire, and Adam from the substance already described to you.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p402/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p402/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p402/r1.claim: Ibn Masud says the molten liquid offered to those seeking relief is melted gold and silver together.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p402/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p402/r2.speaker: كعب
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p402/r2.claim: Ka'b identifies the people described with this fate as those who consistently maintain the five prayers in congregation.

AKHFASH:v2p430/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p430/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p430/r2.claim: وقل الحق من ربكم means Say: it is the truth from your Lord, with هو understood.

AKHFASH:v2p430/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p430/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p430/r3.claim: وساءت مرتفقا means the abode is a bad resting place.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p267/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p267/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p267/r1.claim: Surādiq is a chamber around a tent; it is also smoke surrounding disbelievers on Judgment Day or the three-branched shade mentioned elsewhere.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p267/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p267/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p267/r2.claim: Muhl means the dregs of oil or what has been melted from copper and lead.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p267/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p267/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p267/r3.claim: Murtafaq means a resting place or seat; irtifāq originally means leaning on one's elbow.

TAB-FULL:v15p245#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p245#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p245#2/r1.claim: أعتدنا means prepared, from the word for provision or readiness; the wrongdoers in this warning are those who disbelieved in their Lord.

TAB-FULL:v15p245#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p245#2/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v15p245#2/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd explicitly glosses the wrongdoers for whom the fire is prepared as unbelievers.

TAB-FULL:v15p245#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p245#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p245#2/r3.claim: The fire’s surādiq is a wall of fire surrounding them like a tent enclosure; the word is illustrated by lines from Ruʾba and Salāma ibn Jandal.

TAB-FULL:v15p245#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p245#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p245#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also interprets the enclosure as a wall of fire.

TAB-FULL:v15p245#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p245#2/r5.speaker: معمر
TAB-FULL:v15p245#2/r5.claim: A report attributed to Maʿmar from an unnamed authority says the enclosure is smoke surrounding unbelievers, like the three-branched shade.

TAB-FULL:v15p245#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p245#2/r6.speaker: يعلى بن أمية
TAB-FULL:v15p245#2/r6.claim: A Prophetic report from Yaʿlā ibn Umayya identifies the sea with Hell and takes the encircling enclosure as the sea in this world; the Prophet swore he would not enter it alive.

TAB-FULL:v15p245#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p245#2/r7.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
TAB-FULL:v15p245#2/r7.claim: A Prophetic report from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī says Hell’s enclosure has four walls, each as thick as a forty-year journey.

TAB-FULL:v15p245/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p245/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p245/r1.claim: Truth comes from God; guidance and misguidance are in His hand, while the Prophet is not to dismiss believers to satisfy the elite.

TAB-FULL:v15p245/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p245/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p245/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says whom God wills to believe believes and whom He wills to disbelieve disbelieves, consistent with the statement that human willing depends on God’s will.

TAB-FULL:v15p245/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p245/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p245/r3.claim: Whoever wishes may believe or disbelieve is a threat and warning, not permission to choose unbelief; the following threat of fire establishes this.

TAB-FULL:v15p245/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p245/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p245/r4.claim: Mujāhid likewise calls the statement a divine threat that cannot be evaded.

TAB-FULL:v15p245/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p245/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v15p245/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd links this threat to 41:40 and says such language is neither appeasement nor a delegation of choice.

TAB-FULL:v15p248#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p248#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p248#2/r1.claim: In the Fire, the wrongdoers’ thirst prompts them to ask for water, but they are given molten-like water.

TAB-FULL:v15p248#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p248#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p248#2/r2.claim: Qatāda relates that Ibn Masʿūd melted a gold-and-silver drinking vessel, then said this was the closest worldly likeness to maḥl.

TAB-FULL:v15p248#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p248#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p248#2/r3.claim: Mujāhid interprets maḥl as pus and black blood, like the sediment of oil.

TAB-FULL:v15p248#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p248#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p248#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās describes maḥl as black like oil or thick like its sediment.

TAB-FULL:v15p248#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p248#2/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v15p248#2/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says Hell’s water is black, as are Hell, its trees, and its inhabitants.

TAB-FULL:v15p248#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p248#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p248#2/r6.claim: Another report from Ibn ʿAbbās calls it thick water like oil sediment.

TAB-FULL:v15p248#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p248#2/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v15p248#2/r7.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says maḥl is something brought to its maximum heat.

TAB-FULL:v15p248#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p248#2/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p248#2/r8.claim: These apparently different descriptions converge: molten lead, gold, or silver reaches extreme heat, and burning it to oil sediment also leaves it at maximum heat.

TAB-FULL:v15p248/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p248/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد
TAB-FULL:v15p248/r1.claim: The Prophet says the fire’s enclosure consists of four walls, each as thick as a forty-year journey; its water is like oil sediment and burns the face when brought near.

TAB-FULL:v15p251/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p251/r1.speaker: المنتجع بن نبهان
TAB-FULL:v15p251/r1.claim: Al-Muntajiʿ ibn Nabḥān describes maḥl as liquid heated to its limit, or a solid melted by fire until it reaches extreme heat, comparing it with molten residue from baking.

TAB-FULL:v15p252#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p252#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p252#2/r1.claim: The drink is evil, and the Fire is a terrible resting place; in Arabic, a place of irtifāq is where one leans or rests on an elbow.

TAB-FULL:v15p252#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p252#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p252#2/r2.claim: An unnamed poet’s line uses مرتفقا for leaning on an elbow; Abū Dhuʾayb likewise describes spending the night leaning on his elbow.

TAB-FULL:v15p252#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p252#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p252#2/r3.claim: Mujāhid interprets مرتفقا as a gathering place.

TAB-FULL:v15p252#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p252#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p252#2/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says he does not know irtifāq to mean gathering in Arabic; its derivation is from elbow or gentleness.

TAB-FULL:v15p252/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p252/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p252/r1.claim: The water they are given sears their faces.

TAB-FULL:v15p252/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p252/r2.speaker: أبو أمامة
TAB-FULL:v15p252/r2.claim: A Prophetic report on 14:17 says the drinker recoils; when brought near it sears his face and scalp, and when swallowed cuts his intestines.

TAB-FULL:v15p252/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p252/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v15p252/r3.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr describes the sequence: the starving inhabitants eat from Zaqqum until facial skin is stripped, then thirst and receive scorching maḥl that burns the exposed flesh.

ZAJJAJ:v3p281#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p281#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p281#2/r1.claim: A suradiq is any enclosure around something, such as a tent curtain or surrounding wall.

ZAJJAJ:v3p281#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p281#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p281#2/r2.claim: Muhl is molten metal; it is also interpreted as oil dregs or wound pus, and the drink scorches faces from its heat.

ZAJJAJ:v3p281#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p281#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p281#2/r3.claim: مرتفقا is a specification and can mean an abode; linguists also define it as a leaning place, witnessed by an unattributed poem.

ZAJJAJ:v3p281/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p281/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p281/r3.claim: The truth is what the Prophet brought from his Lord; believe or disbelieve is a warning, not a command, and the following verses explain each group's fate.

ZAJJAJ:v3p281/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p281/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p281/r4.claim: أعتدنا means prepared as permanent provision; عتاد is something fixed and lasting.

SULAMI:v1p410#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p410#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p410#2/r1.claim: God disclosed the paths of truth and reality; those granted divine success are guided to faith, while those abandoned to misguidance follow the distant path of unbelief.

THALABI:v6p166/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p166/r17.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p166/r17.claim: Al-haqq may be nominative as a quoted declaration, as predicate of an omitted subject meaning 'it is the truth,' or as a subject whose predicate is 'from your Lord.'

THALABI:v6p166/r18.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p166/r18.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p166/r18.claim: The truth includes the Qur'an, faith, and Muhammad's message; guidance and misguidance are God's decision, and the Prophet is not to expel believers for elite company.

THALABI:v6p167/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p167/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p167/r1.claim: The invitation to believe or disbelieve is a warning and threat, not permission to choose freely, like the command to do as one wishes.

THALABI:v6p167/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p167/r10.speaker: سلامة بن جندل
THALABI:v6p167/r10.claim: Salama ibn Jandal's line uses musardaq for an enclosed roof or building.

THALABI:v6p167/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p167/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p167/r11.claim: Here the enclosure is smoke surrounding disbelievers at resurrection, as in the passage about a shade with three branches in al-Mursalat.

THALABI:v6p167/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p167/r12.speaker: رسول الله
THALABI:v6p167/r12.claim: Abu Muslim transmits from Abu Sa'id that the water like molten dregs is like oil sediment, and its heat makes facial skin fall when brought near.

THALABI:v6p167/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p167/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p167/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas describes al-muhl as thick water like the sediment of oil.

THALABI:v6p167/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p167/r14.speaker: الأعمش
THALABI:v6p167/r14.claim: Al-A'mash glosses al-muhl as the squeezed residue of oil.

THALABI:v6p167/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p167/r15.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v6p167/r15.claim: Mujahid glosses al-muhl as pus and blood.

THALABI:v6p167/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p167/r16.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v6p167/r16.claim: Al-Dahhak says al-muhl is black water, since Hell, its water and trees, and its inhabitants are black.

THALABI:v6p167/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p167/r17.speaker: أبو عبيدة
THALABI:v6p167/r17.claim: Abu Ubayda defines al-muhl as anything melted from the earth's minerals.

THALABI:v6p167/r18.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p167/r18.speaker: ابن مسعود
THALABI:v6p167/r18.claim: Qatada recounts that Ibn Masud demonstrated al-muhl by melting a gold-and-silver cup in a trench fire until it foamed and liquefied.

THALABI:v6p167/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p167/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p167/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says whoever God wills to believe believes, and whoever He wills to disbelieve disbelieves, citing that human willing depends on God's will.

THALABI:v6p167/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p167/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p167/r3.claim: A'tadna means prepared or made ready from atad, meaning equipment; the fire is for the wrongdoers, meaning disbelievers.

THALABI:v6p167/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p167/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p167/r4.claim: The verse proves that Hell is already created: if it were not existing and prepared, the report would be false, which is impossible of God.

THALABI:v6p167/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p167/r5.speaker: رسول الله
THALABI:v6p167/r5.claim: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri reports that the Fire's enclosure consists of four thick walls, each forty years' journey across.

THALABI:v6p167/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p167/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p167/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says the enclosure is a wall of fire.

THALABI:v6p167/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p167/r7.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v6p167/r7.claim: Al-Kalbi calls it a neck emerging from the Fire that surrounds disbelievers like an enclosure.

THALABI:v6p167/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p167/r8.speaker: القتيبي
THALABI:v6p167/r8.claim: Al-Qutaybi defines saradiq as the chamber erected around a tent.

THALABI:v6p167/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p167/r9.speaker: رؤبة
THALABI:v6p167/r9.claim: Ruba's line describes the canopy of glory as spread over a person, supporting the word saradiq.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r1.claim: Although phrased as a choice to believe or disbelieve, the statement is a threat and warning.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r10.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r10.claim: Molten fluid may mean pus and blood.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r11.claim: Molten fluid may mean the dregs of oil.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r12.claim: Molten fluid may be anything melted until liquefied.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r13.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r13.claim: Molten fluid may be water whose heat has reached its limit; a cited line uses مهلا كريها for a hot, foul liquid.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r14.claim: Calling this water an answer to their plea for help is ironic because it is ruinous to drink.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r15.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r15.claim: مرتفقا may mean a gathering place, related to companionship.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r16.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r16.claim: مرتفقا may mean a dwelling or place to stay, from the root of resting on something.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r17.claim: A further explanation connects مرتفقا with comfort or ease.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r18.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r18.claim: مرتفقا may mean a place to recline or rest, from مرفق; Abu Dhu'ayb's poem supplies poetic evidence.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r2.claim: One point is that people's faith does not benefit God and their disbelief cannot harm Him.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas paraphrases the challenge as: whoever wants Paradise should believe, and whoever wants the Fire may disbelieve.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r4.claim: Alternatively, people may expose themselves to Paradise through faith or to the Fire through disbelief.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r5.claim: The suradiq is a wall of fire surrounding the disbelievers.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r6.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r6.claim: The suradiq may be smoke and flame before the people reach Hell, connected with 77:30-31.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r7.claim: The suradiq may be the sea that encircles the world.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r8.claim: A report from Ya'la ibn Umayya says the Prophet called the sea Hell, recited the surrounding-fire verse, and swore that while he lived he would never enter it or be touched by a drop from it; no grading is stated.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p302/r9.claim: Suradiq is a Persian loanword, originally سرادر.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p304/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p304/r1.speaker: أبو ذؤيب
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p304/r1.claim: Abu Dhu'ayb's verse uses مرتفقا for reclining or resting, supporting the interpretation of مرتفق as a place to lean or rest.

QUSHAYRI:v2p218/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p218/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p218/r1.claim: The permission to believe or disbelieve is the utmost threat: faith benefits believers themselves, while punishment falls on deniers.

QUSHAYRI:v2p218/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p218/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p218/r2.claim: God gains no benefit from universal faith and suffers no loss from universal disbelief.

QUSHAYRI:v2p218/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p218/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p218/r3.claim: The great punishment occupies the damned with pain so they cannot attend to regret for having missed the truth.

QUSHAYRI:v2p218/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p218/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p218/r4.claim: The Real is too generous to punish someone who is accused or blamed on His account.

QUSHAYRI:v2p218/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p218/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p218/r5.claim: Recognizing who calls their resting place evil might console the damned, but they fail to recognize the speaker.

QUSHAYRI:v2p218/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p218/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p218/r6.claim: Paradise's gardens are good for its inhabitants, while the Fire's enclosure surrounds its inhabitants; God gains nothing from either punishment or reward.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p602#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p602#2/r1.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p602#2/r1.claim: The Prophet is to address people of every worldly rank who come to him.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p602#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p602#2/r2.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p602#2/r2.claim: The addressees are those asking the Prophet to dismiss the poor and give them a closer seat so they might believe.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p602#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p602#2/r3.speaker: الكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p602#2/r3.claim: “The truth is from your Lord” means Islam is the truth from your Lord.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p602#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p602#2/r4.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p602#2/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash supplies “it is”: say, “It is the truth.”

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p602#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p602#2/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق وقتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p602#2/r5.claim: Abu Ishaq says the message brought to them is the truth; Qatada identifies it as the Quran.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p602#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p602#2/r6.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p602#2/r6.claim: “Whoever wills may believe and whoever wills may disbelieve” is a threat.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p602#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p602#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p602#2/r7.claim: Qatada says God has made the matter clear and then offered a choice, a choice intended as a threat.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p602#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p602#2/r8.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p602#2/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains the apparent choice as warning, not a command whose alternatives would both count as obedience; the following verses specify each group's fate, the majority view.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p604/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p604/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p604/r1.claim: “We have prepared” means made ready; “the wrongdoers” here are those who worship someone besides God.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p604/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p604/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p604/r2.claim: A saradiq is anything enclosing or surrounding something, such as cloth or a wall, and is most often used for a pavilion.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p604/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p604/r3.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p604/r3.claim: Al-Layth describes a saradiq as an enclosed chamber made from thick woven wool, used around royal pavilions.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p604/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p604/r4.speaker: رؤبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p604/r4.claim: Ru'ba's line uses “saradiq” for an expanse or canopy of glory spread over someone.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p604/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p604/r5.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p604/r5.claim: Al-Azhari also uses the word for rising dust or conspicuous smoke surrounding something.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p604/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p604/r6.speaker: لبيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p604/r6.claim: Labid applies “saradiq” to a covering raised around camels on a windy day.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p604/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p604/r7.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري عن النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p604/r7.claim: The Prophet said Hell's enclosure has four walls, each wall a forty-year journey in thickness.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p604/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p604/r8.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p604/r8.claim: Al-Kalbi identifies the enclosure as smoke surrounding disbelievers on Judgment Day, and applies the same image to two other verses; Abu Ubayda and Ibn Qutayba choose this view.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r1.claim: Those suffering will seek rescue from their punishment and intense thirst.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r10.speaker: ابن عباس رواية سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says it is oil sediment; al-Walibi and al-Awfi report similarly.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r11.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r11.claim: Mujahid says muhl means pus and blood.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r12.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r12.claim: Ata reports Ibn Abbas's interpretation as the sediment of tar.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r13.speaker: قتادة والحسن عن ابن مسعود
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r13.claim: Asked about muhl, Ibn Masud melted gold and silver together and said the bubbling molten mixture was the closest worldly likeness of Hell's drink.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r14.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r14.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r14.claim: Al-Zajjaj chooses the molten-metal interpretation—lead, brass, or silver—because such metals reach extreme heat when melted.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r2.speaker: أبو عبيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r2.claim: Abu Ubayd defines muhl as any smelted metal.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r3.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r3.claim: A report quotes Abu Bakr's instruction to bury him in two garments, saying they are for muhl and dust; Abu Ubayda interprets muhl there as pus and suppuration.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r4.claim: Abu Amr says muhl in Abu Bakr's report means pus, while elsewhere it means sediment of oil.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r5.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r5.claim: Al-Layth calls muhl a kind of tar and gives a related verb for coating a camel with it.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r6.speaker: ابن شميل عن شمر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r6.claim: Ibn Shumayl says muhl is like heated embers or clay when it becomes very hot and visibly waves.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r7.speaker: العامرية
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r7.claim: The Banu Amir dialect uses muhl for poison.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r8.claim: Al-Wahidi counts six lexical senses of muhl.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r9.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري عن النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p606/r9.claim: The Prophet glossed the drink “like muhl” as the sediment of oil.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p609/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p609/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p609/r1.claim: The verb for roasting meat is shawaytu; ashwaytu means roasting specifically for oneself, and inshawa and ishtawa are also used for being roasted.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p609/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p609/r2.speaker: لبيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p609/r2.claim: Labid's line uses a related form for roasting at night.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p609/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p609/r3.speaker: الخدري عن النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p609/r3.claim: The Prophet said that when the drink is brought close, the skin of the drinker's face falls into it.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p609/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p609/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p609/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says it scorches the face until its flesh falls away.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p609/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p609/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p609/r5.claim: “What a bad drink” refers to the water just described; “a bad resting place” describes Hell and is accusative as a specification.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p609/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p609/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p609/r6.claim: The phrase means how bad the thing they rely on is.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p609/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p609/r7.speaker: مجاهد، وعطاء، والزجاج، وابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p609/r7.claim: They gloss “resting place” as gathering, place, dwelling, or sitting place; al-Wahidi says these senses converge on a place where one finds use or comfort.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p609/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p609/r8.speaker: ابن السكيت
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p609/r8.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit explains the word as a recliner, from leaning on one's elbow; a place where one stays and sits is a place of rest.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p609/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p609/r9.speaker: الهذلي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p609/r9.claim: The Hudhali line “I slept at ease while lying on my elbow” supports the sense of reclining.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:29-31/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:29-31/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:29-31/r1.claim: The truth from God means Islam and the Qur'an; “believe or disbelieve” is an apparent choice whose meaning is a threat.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:29-31/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:29-31/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:29-31/r2.claim: The wrongdoers who worship anything besides God face a fire surrounded by smoke that encloses unbelievers at resurrection.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:29-31/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:29-31/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:29-31/r3.claim: The drink offered in response to cries for relief is molten iron or lead whose heat burns away the face's flesh; it is a wretched drink and resting place.

JISHUMI:v6p4396/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4396/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4396/r8.claim: Surādiq is an enclosure or curtain around a tent; mahl is the residue of oil or molten copper.

JISHUMI:v6p4396/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4396/r9.speaker: رؤبة
JISHUMI:v6p4396/r9.claim: His line about the tent of glory with its extended surādiq witnesses the word's sense of an enclosing canopy.

JISHUMI:v6p4397/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4397/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4397/r1.claim: Marfiq is something that benefits or supports; a martafaq is a resting place or seat named for leaning on the elbow, or for ease and benefit.

JISHUMI:v6p4397/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4397/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4397/r2.claim: ‘Whoever wills, let him believe’ is a jussive threat in the form of a command, making the threat harsher because it commands what brings humiliation.

JISHUMI:v6p4397/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4397/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4397/r3.claim: The nominative الحق may be quotation, a predicate of an omitted ‘it is,’ or a subject whose predicate is من ربكم; ‘bad as a resting place’ supplies Hell as the unstated subject.

JISHUMI:v6p4403/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4403/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4403/r1.claim: God's words never fail in their threat, contrary to the Murjiʾa.

JISHUMI:v6p4403/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4403/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4403/r10.claim: The Fire for wrongdoers means grave sinners are among the people of Hell, contrary to the Murjiʾa.

JISHUMI:v6p4403/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4403/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4403/r11.claim: Following desire and disbelief are acts of the people who commit them.

JISHUMI:v6p4403/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4403/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4403/r2.claim: There is no escape except to God, so a rational person should turn to Him and rely on Him.

JISHUMI:v6p4403/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4403/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4403/r3.claim: Adornment should be through religion rather than worldly display.

JISHUMI:v6p4403/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4403/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4403/r4.claim: Worship should be performed seeking God's face.

JISHUMI:v6p4403/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4403/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4403/r5.claim: One should not leave religious people for corrupt people because of wealth.

JISHUMI:v6p4403/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4403/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4403/r6.claim: No one may be obeyed in disobedience to God.

JISHUMI:v6p4403/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4403/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4403/r7.claim: The religion is true and falsehood is not from God; this explains 'from your Lord.'

JISHUMI:v6p4403/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4403/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4403/r8.claim: The wording that the Fire is prepared indicates that Paradise and Hell are already created, against Abu Hashim.

JISHUMI:v6p4403/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4403/r9.speaker: أبو هاشم
JISHUMI:v6p4403/r9.claim: Abu Hashim interprets the preparation as a promise that God will create the Fire; past tense elsewhere can express certainty about a future event.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p167#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p167#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p167#2/r1.claim: God prepared the Fire for unbelieving wrongdoers; a sarādaq is a surrounding chamber or enclosure.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p167#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p167#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p167#2/r2.claim: Abu Saʿīd reports that the Fire's enclosure has four thick walls, each as long as a forty-year journey.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p167#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p167#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p167#2/r3.claim: He says the enclosure is a wall of fire.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p167#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p167#2/r4.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p167#2/r4.claim: He says a neck emerges from the Fire and surrounds unbelievers like an enclosure.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p167#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p167#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p167#2/r5.claim: Another view says the enclosure is smoke surrounding unbelievers, identified with the three-branched shade.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p167/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p167/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p167/r1.claim: The truth just described, including faith and the Qur'an, is from the Lord; guidance and misguidance rest with God, not the Prophet.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p167/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p167/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p167/r2.claim: The command to believe or disbelieve is a threat, like the command to do as one wishes.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p167/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p167/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p167/r3.claim: Another interpretation says the Prophet must not dismiss believers to satisfy elite preferences: people may choose belief or disbelief, but disbelief brings the surrounding Fire and belief brings promised reward.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p167/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p167/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p167/r4.claim: He says whoever God wills to believe believes, and whoever He wills to disbelieve disbelieves.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p168#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p168#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p168#2/r1.claim: The drink's heat cooks and scorches faces.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p168#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p168#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p168#2/r2.claim: He glosses the Fire as a bad dwelling place.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p168#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p168#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p168#2/r3.claim: He glosses it as a gathering place.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p168#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p168#2/r4.speaker: عطاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p168#2/r4.claim: He glosses it as a station or abode.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p168#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p168#2/r5.speaker: القتيبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p168#2/r5.claim: He glosses it as a sitting place; the word originally means a place to recline.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p168/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p168/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p168/r1.claim: Abu Saʿīd reports that the drink is like oil dregs and drops the skin of the face when brought near.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p168/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p168/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p168/r2.claim: He describes mihl as thick water like oil sediment.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p168/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p168/r3.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p168/r3.claim: He says mihl is pus and blood.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p168/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p168/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p168/r4.claim: He heated gold and silver until they melted, then said the result was the closest likeness of mihl.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r12.claim: The truth from the Lord may mean the Quran itself, or the Prophet's refusal to obey the elites and his patience with the believers.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r13.speaker: قعنب وأبو السمال
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r13.claim: Qunab and Abu al-Sammal read qul with a fatḥa on the lām; Abu Hatim judges this poor Arabic.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r14.claim: The commands to believe or disbelieve are a threat: each person is challenged to choose what he will find with God.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r15.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r15.claim: One group construes the choice as governed by God's will: whom He wills to believe believes, and whom He wills to disbelieve disbelieves.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r16.claim: Ibn Atiyya accepts that construal, while explaining that faith or disbelief is the person's due and that human acquisition grounds reward and punishment.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r17.speaker: الحسن وعيسى الثقفي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r17.claim: Al-Hasan and Isa al-Thaqafi read the lām in both commands with kasra.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r18.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r18.claim: Aʿtadna derives from ʿatād, something prepared and ready at hand; surādq is an enclosing wall or tent-like surround.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r1.speaker: رؤبة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r1.claim: Ruʾba's verse uses surādq for an enclosure, supporting the word's concrete sense.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r10.speaker: أبو سعيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r10.claim: Abu Saʿid reports from the Prophet that muhl is the dregs of oil heated to its limit.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r11.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r11.claim: Other explanations of muhl include any liquid heated to its extreme, molten gold, silver, or lead, and a mixture of pus and blood.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r12.claim: Ibn Masud compared muhl with molten metal by melting a gold or silver vessel and showing its colors to people in Kufa.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r13.claim: A prophetic report describes the drink burning a disbeliever's face before it is swallowed and cutting his intestines after drinking.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r14.claim: Murtfaq generally means something from which comfort is sought; the narrower sense is a reclining place, while Mujahid calls it a gathering place and al-Tabari rejects that gloss.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r2.speaker: سلامة بن جندل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r2.claim: Salama b. Jandal uses musardaq for an enclosed structure, another poetic witness to the word.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines surādq broadly as anything that surrounds something.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r4.claim: Ibn Atiyya considers surādq more specific than al-Zajjaj's definition of anything enclosing anything.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says Hell's enclosure is a wall of fire; another group says it is smoke surrounding the disbelievers.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r6.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r6.claim: A group interprets the enclosure as smoke surrounding the disbelievers and connects it with the three-branched shade in al-Mursalat.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r7.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r7.claim: Another group places the enclosure in this world and identifies it with the sea; a report from the Prophet through Yaʿla b. Umayya says the sea is Hell.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r8.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r8.claim: A report from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri says Hell's enclosure has four walls, each forty years' journey wide.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p513/r9.claim: Yughāthū means they are given something that serves as relief, as in a poet's ironic description of a painful blow as a greeting.

TABRISI:18:28-29#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:28-29#2/r1.speaker: أبو ذؤيب
TABRISI:18:28-29#2/r1.claim: Abu Dhuʾayb's verse of the night traveler leaning on an elbow is cited as evidence for مرتفق meaning a place or posture of leaning.

TABRISI:18:28-29#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:28-29#3/r4.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:18:28-29#3/r4.claim: The declaration ‘the truth is from your Lord’ may mean that the revelation is true and came from God rather than from the Prophet himself.

TABRISI:18:28-29#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:28-29#3/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:28-29#3/r5.claim: Another gloss says the proof has appeared, truth is clear, and doubt has been removed.

TABRISI:18:28-29#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:28-29#3/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:28-29#3/r6.claim: ‘Let whoever wishes believe and whoever wishes disbelieve’ is a threat, not permission: each person chooses what harms or benefits himself, not God.

TABRISI:18:28-29#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:28-29#3/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:28-29#3/r7.claim: The imperative form works as a threat because the person threatened is effectively being ordered to bring humiliation on himself.

TABRISI:18:28-29#4/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:28-29#4/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:18:28-29#4/r1.claim: The fire's سرادق is a wall of fire surrounding the condemned; Qatada alternatively takes it as the smoke and flame reaching them before the fire, while Abu Muslim treats it as an image of encirclement on every side.

TABRISI:18:28-29#4/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:28-29#4/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:28-29#4/r2.claim: Those suffering thirst and heat who beg for relief are given water like molten metal; Ibn Masʿud identifies it as melted lead, copper, or brass.

TABRISI:18:28-29#4/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:28-29#4/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:28-29#4/r3.claim: Other reported explanations of مهل are oil scum that burns the scalp when approached, oil dregs, pus and blood, liquid at extreme heat, or black water in a wholly black Hell; authorities include Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, and al-Dahhak.

TABRISI:18:28-29#4/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:28-29#4/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:28-29#4/r4.claim: The water scorches and cooks faces as it nears them; it is called relief only because the text pairs it with the word for being given relief.

TABRISI:18:28-29#4/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:28-29#4/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:18:28-29#4/r5.claim: The fire is a wretched place to lean or gather in; Mujahid derives مرتفق from companionship and assembly.

TABRISI:18:28-29#4/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:28-29#4/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:18:28-29#4/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas and ʿAṭāʾ gloss مرتفق as a lodging or settled abode.

TABRISI:18:28-29/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:28-29/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:28-29/r5.claim: The word فرط means exceeding the truth and going beyond proper limits; سرادق is the surrounding tent or cloth enclosure.

TABRISI:18:28-29/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:28-29/r6.speaker: رؤبة
TABRISI:18:28-29/r6.claim: Ruʾba's line about a canopy of glory is cited to attest that سرادق means an enclosing pavilion or canopy.

TABRISI:18:28-29/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:28-29/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:28-29/r7.claim: The word مهل can mean the thick residue of oil, molten copper, or another melted metal; مرتفق is a place to lean on, from leaning on one's elbow, and may also suggest a place of benefit.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r1.claim: The truth is the message the Prophet brought from his Lord.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r10.claim: One view makes the surrounding barrier a curtain of fire; a report from Abu Sa'id says it has four dense walls, each a forty-year journey.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r11.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r11.claim: Another report describes a tongue of fire that emerges from Hell and encircles the unbelievers until judgment ends.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r12.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r12.claim: A second view identifies the barrier as smoke surrounding unbelievers, the three-branched shade mentioned at 77:30.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r13.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r13.claim: One of seven interpretations of muhl is thick water like the sediment of oil.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r14.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r14.claim: Muhl can mean anything melted until liquefied.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r15.speaker: أبو عبيدة والزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r15.claim: They explain muhl as anything melted, such as copper or lead.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r16.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r16.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r16.claim: One report from Mujahid defines it as black pus and blood like the dregs of oil.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r2.claim: One interpretation of whoever wills may believe is whoever God wills may believe.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r3.claim: Another interpretation is that this is a threat and warning, not an imperative.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r4.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r4.claim: A third meaning is that faith does not benefit God and disbelief does not harm Him; some say this expresses divine self-sufficiency rather than licensing unbelief.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r5.claim: أعتدنا means We prepared and made ready; he refers to the earlier discussion at 12:31.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r6.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r6.claim: The wrongdoers meant here are unbelievers.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r7.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r7.claim: A saradiq is anything surrounding something, such as the tent curtain or a surrounding wall.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r8.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r8.claim: A saradiq is the chamber around a tent.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r9.speaker: أبو منصور اللغوي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p134/r9.claim: He says saradiq is a Persian loanword, originally saradar, meaning vestibule; al-Farazdaq's verse uses the word.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p135/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p135/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p135/r1.claim: A second report from Mujahid says muhl is silver and lead being melted.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p135/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p135/r10.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p135/r10.claim: A fifth meaning is a place from which one seeks ease, but ease is denied there; the senses converge on what one leans on.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p135/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p135/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p135/r2.claim: Muhl is something whose heat has reached its limit.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p135/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p135/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p135/r3.claim: Another view defines it as pus; Mughib ibn Sumayy explains it as the cooked mixture of the people's sweat, tears, blood, and pus, offered as Hell's first drink.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p135/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p135/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p135/r4.claim: A seventh view takes muhl as ash shaken from bread after it comes out of an oven.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p135/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p135/r5.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p135/r5.claim: When the drink is brought near, the skin of the face falls away from its burning heat.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p135/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p135/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p135/r6.claim: One meaning of مرتفقا is a dwelling.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p135/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p135/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p135/r7.claim: Another meaning is a gathering place.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p135/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p135/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p135/r8.claim: A third meaning is a place to lean or rest one's elbow; he cites poetry as evidence, and al-Zajjaj parses it as a specification of manner.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p135/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p135/r9.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p135/r9.claim: A fourth meaning is a seat or assembly.

RAZI-FULL:v21p101#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p101#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p101#2/r1.claim: One account of the passage's order says it answers wealthy leaders who conditioned belief on expelling the poor: acceptance benefits them, refusal harms them, and social status is irrelevant.

RAZI-FULL:v21p101#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p101#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p101#2/r2.claim: A second account identifies the truth from God as the command to keep company with poor believers and disregard worldly leaders.

RAZI-FULL:v21p101#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p101#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p101#2/r3.claim: A third account connects the passage to the freedom to believe or disbelieve and God's refusal to expel believers to attract unbelieving elites.

RAZI-FULL:v21p101#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p101#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p101#2/r4.claim: The objection that expelling the poor would sacrifice a small harm to them to prevent the greater harm of unbelief is rejected: belief conditional on avoiding the poor is ugly hypocrisy.

RAZI-FULL:v21p101#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p101#3/r1.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v21p101#3/r1.claim: The Mu'tazila take the invitation to believe or disbelieve as explicit proof that faith, disbelief, obedience, and sin are left to human choice.

RAZI-FULL:v21p101#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p101#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p101#3/r2.claim: Razi argues that actions require intention and choice, but every intention cannot depend on an earlier one indefinitely; the chain must end in a will God creates necessarily in a person.

RAZI-FULL:v21p101#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p101#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p101#3/r3.claim: When the decisive will exists, the action follows necessarily; when it is absent, the action does not occur, leaving humans compelled in the form of choosers.

RAZI-FULL:v21p101#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p101#3/r4.speaker: أبو حامد الغزالي
RAZI-FULL:v21p101#3/r4.claim: Al-Ghazali presents the objection that people directly experience being able to act if they will and to refrain if they will.

RAZI-FULL:v21p101#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p101#3/r5.speaker: أبو حامد الغزالي
RAZI-FULL:v21p101#3/r5.claim: Al-Ghazali replies that people do not choose whether their will itself arises; it appears without an earlier will, and action follows it necessarily, so both are from God.

RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r1.claim: The verse shows that an action cannot issue from an agent without intention and motive.

RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r10.speaker: أبو عبيدة والأخفش
RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r10.claim: Abu Ubayda and al-Akhfash define molten metal as anything melted from gold, copper, or silver.

RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r11.claim: Other glosses of the molten drink are pus and blood, or a kind of tar.

RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r12.claim: They may ask for water because they are thirsty; the passage compares this with being given drink from a boiling spring.

RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r13.claim: Alternatively, they may seek water to cool themselves, but are given tar that covers their bodies like a garment.

RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r2.claim: Ali says the imperative here is a threat and warning, not a grant of choice.

RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r3.claim: God neither benefits from believers' faith nor suffers from unbelievers' disbelief; benefit and harm return to people themselves.

RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r4.claim: The passage moves from describing truth, falsehood, faith, and disbelief to threats for disbelief and false deeds and promises for faith and good deeds.

RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r5.claim: The wrongdoers are those who misplace worship and pride, rejecting truth because poor people accepted it; God has prepared Hell for them.

RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r6.claim: A suradīq is a barrier around a tent; the image means the fire encloses them on every side with no escape or opening.

RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r7.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r7.claim: Some interpret the enclosing barrier as smoke like the three-branched shade, surrounding the unbelievers before they enter the fire.

RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r8.speaker: حديث مرفوع
RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r8.claim: A prophetic report glosses the water like molten metal as the dregs of oil.

RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v21p102/r9.claim: Ibn Mas'ud heated a residue taken from the treasury until it glowed and identified it as molten metal.

RAZI-FULL:v21p103/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p103/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p103/r1.claim: An unnamed poetic line mocks the exchange by calling a painful blow a greeting.

RAZI-FULL:v21p103/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p103/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p103/r2.claim: The drink is especially vile because a drink should relieve heat, but this one burns bodies intensely.

RAZI-FULL:v21p103/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p103/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p103/r3.claim: One interpretation of a bad resting place is that Hell is a vile gathering and abode for its companions, unbelievers and devils, unlike the good companionship and abode of Paradise.

RAZI-FULL:v21p103/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p103/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p103/r4.claim: Another interpretation makes مرتفقا a resting place or reclining place, since a marfiq is named for what one leans on.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r1.claim: Abu Saʿid reports that the Fire’s canopy has four thick walls, each a forty-year journey; al-Tirmidhi grades the report hasan, sahih, gharib.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r10.claim: The reports support the range of lexical interpretations, which the author says are all intended; Arabic dictionaries likewise record molten copper, lead, oil dregs, pus, and exudate.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r11.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r11.claim: Mujahid takes martefaqan as a place where people gather.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas says martefaqan means a dwelling.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r13.speaker: عطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r13.claim: Ata interprets it as a place of residence; another view calls it a bed, and al-Qutaybi a gathering place.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r14.claim: These senses are close, and the root means a place to lean on an elbow; irtafaqa means to rest on the elbow.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r2.claim: The report indicates that the canopy is smoke or fire above the disbelievers, with walls as described.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says mahl is thick water like the dregs of oil.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r4.claim: Mujahid identifies mahl as pus and blood.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r5.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak calls it black water, since Hell, its water, its trees, and its inhabitants are black.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة وابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r6.claim: Abu Ubayda, with a similar report from Ibn Masud, describes molten metals of the earth boiling together as mahl.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r7.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says mahl is liquid at its hottest, and also describes it as a kind of tar; another view calls it poison. The author says these meanings are close.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r8.claim: A Tirmidhi report compares the drink to oil lees and says the skin of the face falls when it is brought near; the compiler notes Rashdin was criticized for weak memory.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r9.speaker: أبو أمامة
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#2/r9.claim: A report on the drink of pus says that when brought near it sears the face and scalp, and when swallowed cuts the intestines; al-Tirmidhi calls it gharib.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#3/r1.claim: An anonymous poetic line uses irtafaqat in the sense of leaning or resting on the elbow.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#3/r2.speaker: أبو ذؤيب الهذلي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29#3/r2.claim: Abu Dhuʾayb says he spent the night resting on his elbow; ṣāb is the bitter sap of a tree.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r1.claim: Al-Haqq may be the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning say: it is the truth; alternatively it is a subject whose predicate is from your Lord.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r10.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r10.claim: Qatadah says it is smoke enclosing the disbelievers, like the smoke described in the verses about a three-branched shade and black smoke.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r11.claim: Another interpretation makes the enclosing barrier the sea surrounding the world.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r12.speaker: يعلى بن أمية
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r12.claim: Yaʿla ibn Umayya reports the Prophet called the sea Hell and recited this verse, saying he would neither enter nor be touched by a drop while alive.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r2.claim: God controls guidance and error: He guides or misleads whom He wills, and truth can be given to the weak and withheld from the rich; the Prophet is not to expel believers for the leaders’ preferences.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r3.claim: The invitation to believe or disbelieve is a threat, not permission to choose either without consequence: disbelief brings the prepared Fire, while faith brings the Garden.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r4.claim: Aʿtadna means prepared, and the wrongdoers meant here are disbelievers who deny the truth.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r5.speaker: الجوهري
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r5.claim: Al-Jawhari defines a suradiq as a canopy stretched over a courtyard, and also uses it for a tent made of coarse hair; al-Ruʾba’s verse pictures glory as a canopy over its owner.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r6.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r6.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrabi takes the fire’s suradiq as its enclosing wall.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the enclosure as a wall of fire.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r8.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r8.claim: Al-Kalbi says a neck emerges from the Fire and surrounds disbelievers like an enclosure.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r9.speaker: القتبي وابن عزيز
QURTUBI-FULL:18:29/r9.claim: Al-Qutaybi and Ibn Aziz identify the suradiq as the surrounding curtain or barrier of a tent.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:29/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:29/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:29/r1.claim: Truth comes from God rather than human desire; the phrase can be parsed as a predicate with an omitted subject or with the preposition circumstantial.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:29/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:29/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:29/r2.claim: The choice to believe or disbelieve does not grant humans independent creation of their acts, since their will is itself not self-willed.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:29/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:29/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:29/r3.claim: The fire's surādıq is a surrounding pavilion-like barrier; others explain it as a surrounding chamber, smoke, or wall of fire.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:29/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:29/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:29/r4.claim: The thirsty will receive molten matter, also likened to oil sediment; its heat will scorch faces when brought to drink.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:29/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:29/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:29/r5.claim: The drink is a second description of the water or a state of the molten substance; it is vile, and Hell is an evil resting place.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:29/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:29/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:29/r6.claim: The root of resting place refers to propping an elbow under the cheek; the wording echoes the good resting place of Paradise, though Hell's people do not recline.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p12/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p12/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p12/r1.claim: The truth from God means either Islam or the Qur'an; “the truth” predicates an omitted “it is.”

NASAFI-FULL:v3p12/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p12/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p12/r2.claim: The command to believe or disbelieve is a threat framed as a choice: once the truth removes excuses, each person chooses salvation or ruin.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p12/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p12/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p12/r3.claim: The threat context restricts the apparent permission in “let whoever wishes disbelieve”; the threatened wrongdoers are unbelievers.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p12/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p12/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p12/r4.claim: The fire's surrounding enclosure (surādiq) is compared to the tent enclosure, or explained as smoke surrounding them before entry, or a wall of fire.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p12/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p12/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p12/r5.claim: Their cry for help is from thirst, and molten dregs of oil scorch their faces; the drink and resting place are dreadful.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p12/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p12/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p12/r6.claim: Calling the fire a resting place is verbal matching with the earlier good resting place; the damned have no actual repose.

QASHANI:18:27-29/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:27-29/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:27-29/r6.claim: The wrongdoers are polytheists veiled from truth; their surrounding fire is the enclosing realm of material natures and forms.

QASHANI:18:27-29/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:27-29/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:27-29/r7.claim: The scalding drink is variously interpreted as foul, blackened, fatty runoff from the damned, their dirty washings, or burning anguish and distress.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r18.speaker: أبو منصور الجواليقي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r18.claim: Abū Manṣūr al-Jawālīqī says surādiq is a Persian loan, originally sarādār meaning vestibule or passageway.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p133/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p133/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p133/r1.claim: Al-Farazdaq’s line uses sarādiq for an enclosure before combat.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p133/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p133/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p133/r2.claim: Mahl is molten mineral material; another view takes it as the dregs of oil. Shawa is meat cooked without broth.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the choice as whoever God wills to have faith believes, while whoever He does not will so does not.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r10.speaker: الماوردي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r10.claim: Al-Māwardī reports that the sarādiq is the sea surrounding the world.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r11.speaker: الكلبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r11.claim: Al-Kalbī says the sarādiq is a neck emerging from Hell and encircling the unbelievers; another view identifies it as smoke.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r12.claim: Their being given relief when they cry is a rhetorical counterstatement, since it is not actual relief from their fire and thirst.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r13.claim: A report says the drink is like cloudy oil: when a face approaches it, its skin falls into it.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās describes the drink as thick, like the sediment of oil.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r15.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r15.claim: Mujāhid identifies the drink as pus and black blood.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r16.speaker: ابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r16.claim: Ibn Jubayr says it is anything molten that has reached extreme heat.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r17.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r17.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī identifies the drink as pus.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r18.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r18.claim: Al-Ḥasan says it is ash shaken out of an oven.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r19.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r19.claim: Another gloss identifies the drink as a kind of pitch.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya reports a group's view that the subject of yashāʾ is God; the imperative form reflects that faith and disbelief follow God's will.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r20.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r20.claim: The clause describing the drink as scorching can be an adjective of water or a circumstantial clause, since water has already been described.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r21.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r21.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r21.claim: Faces are singled out because they are close to the heat as the drinkers drink; alternatively, faces represent their whole bodies, which it cooks.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r3.speaker: أبو السمال قعنب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r3.claim: Abū al-Sammāl Qanab reads qul al-ḥaqqa with the lām fatḥa wherever the phrase occurs; Abū Ḥātim judges this poor Arabic.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r4.speaker: أبو السمال قعنب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r4.claim: He also reads the lām with ḍamma, apparently assimilating it to the preceding qāf vowel.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r5.speaker: أبو السمال قعنب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r5.claim: He reads al-ḥaqqa in the accusative as an adjective of an understood verbal noun, with min attached to an implied phrase.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r6.speaker: الحسن وعيسى الثقفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan and ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī read both command lām vowels as kasra.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r7.claim: The passage first names the punishment for unbelievers and then the reward for believers, prioritizing the unbelievers because the address is to them and follows their request.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r8.claim: A second Arabic ordering principle places the first item in a division with the first item already mentioned, and the second with the second.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168#2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the surrounding sarādiq as a wall of fire.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r14.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r14.claim: If al-ḥaqq is the predicate of an omitted subject, Ibn ʿAṭiyya supplies this truth as either the Qurʾān or the refusal to obey the listeners and the command to remain with believers.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r15.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r15.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes al-ḥaqq as predicate of an omitted subject: truth has come, excuses are gone, and people must choose salvation or ruin.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r16.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r16.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk identifies the truth from the Lord as divine oneness.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r17.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r17.claim: Muqātil identifies the truth from the Lord as the Qurʾān.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r18.speaker: مكي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r18.claim: Makkī says guidance, success, and abandonment are all from God, who guides or leaves people to disbelieve; the Messenger controls none of this.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r19.speaker: الكرماني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r19.claim: Al-Kirmānī glosses the truth as Islam and the Qurʾān.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r20.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r20.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes the wording that sounds like a command to choose as a threat and warning.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r21.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r21.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r21.claim: Al-Suddī says the choice is abrogated by the statement that people will only will what God wills; the author calls this weak.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r22.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r22.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r22.claim: The grammatical subject of yashāʾ in the choice clause is the person denoted by man.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r1.claim: The mention of faces can stand for the whole body, so the drink cooks all their skin, as in the cited description of skin being renewed.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r10.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r10.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī reads the phrase as a failed request for comfort: whoever seeks comfort from Hell will not find it.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r11.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya gives a meaning close to Ibn al-Anbārī's interpretation.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r12.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya's apparent meaning is whatever thing people seek for comfort by reclining or otherwise.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r13.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r13.claim: Al-Rāzī takes it as the worst of companions and the worst place for companionship.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r2.claim: The omitted object of condemnation is the drink itself, namely the water they are given.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r3.claim: The pronoun in sāʾat refers to Hell.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the place of rest as a dwelling.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r5.speaker: عطاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r5.claim: ʿAṭāʾ interprets the place as a lodging or settlement.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r6.speaker: القتبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r6.claim: Al-Qutaybī says it means a sitting place or gathering room.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r7.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r7.claim: Mujāhid glosses it as a gathering place; al-Ṭabarī denies that this has a known meaning, but Abū Ḥayyān says Mujāhid means companionship, from rifqa.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r8.claim: Abū ʿUbayda interprets it as a couch or reclining place.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r9.speaker: الزجاج والزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p169/r9.claim: Al-Zajjāj and al-Zamakhsharī connect the word with leaning on an elbow, but al-Zamakhsharī says the parallel wording is stylistic since Hell affords no reclining.

SAMIN-DURR:18:29#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:29#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:29#2/r1.claim: من may be conditional, the apparent reading, or relative with the fāʾ resembling a conditional construction.

SAMIN-DURR:18:29#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:29#2/r10.speaker: الراغب
